newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee eases mildly against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee eases mildly against forward dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee eased mildly against the forward dollar on Tuesday but dealers said premiums are expected to soften further.
January dollars were quoted at 67/69 paise in late morning trade, up from 66/68 paise opening, dealers said.
Other maturities reflected the same trend.
"There is some interest in covering (forward dollar requirements) as the premiums are very attractive," a dealer at a foreign bank said. Some banks were buying December dollars.
"It is only a correction, the general trend is still down," said a dealer at another bank.
"Forwards are stagnant at current levels," said a dealer.
He said exporters were selling far forwards for better returns, affecting premiums on longer maturities.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 3.23 percent on Monday compared with Friday's close of 3.46 percent.
The chief dealer at a state-run bank said this was the right level. "Premiums should be in the 3.25-4.0 percent band, taking into account the interest differentials," he said.
The spot market was dull on Tuesday, the rupee quoted at 35.81 against the dollar.
"There are only sellers in the market," said a dealer.
